events.text: A mud fort rises on Golconda's shepherds' hill under the Kakatiyas.
Quli Qutb Shah makes Golconda the capital of a new kingdom.
Hussain Sagar lake is built, linking the future twin cities.
Purana Pul, the first bridge over the Musi, opens.
Charminar is built and the new city of Hyderabad is laid out around it.
Badshahi Ashurkhana, the royal mourning hall, is completed.
Work begins on Mecca Masjid.
Toli Masjid rises at Karwan.
After an eight-month siege, Golconda falls to the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb.
Work begins on Chowmahalla Palace, later the Nizams' seat.
The British Residency is built at Koti.
Secunderabad is founded as a British cantonment.
The railway reaches Secunderabad.
Falaknuma Palace is completed on its hill.
The great Musi flood kills thousands; the city is rebuilt with planning and dams.
Osmania University is founded.
Osman Sagar reservoir and the High Court are completed.
Himayat Sagar reservoir is completed.
Moazzam Jahi Market opens.

eras.title: Capital city
eras.sub: Joining India, then capital of Andhra Pradesh

events.text: Hyderabad State joins the Indian Union.
Salar Jung Museum opens to the public.
Hyderabad becomes the capital of Andhra Pradesh.
ECIL is set up; the north-east grows around it.
Birla Mandir opens on Naubath Pahad.
The Buddha statue is installed in Hussain Sagar.
Cyber Towers opens and HITEC City begins.
The Indian School of Business opens at Gachibowli.
Gachibowli's stadiums are built for the National Games.
Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) is formed.
Rajiv Gandhi International Airport opens at Shamshabad.
Telangana becomes a state with Hyderabad as its capital.
Hyderabad Metro opens between Miyapur and Nagole.
Durgam Cheruvu's cable bridge opens.
The new Secretariat and the 125 ft Ambedkar statue open.
Charlapalli rail terminal opens.
GHMC is split into three corporations: GHMC, Cyberabad and Malkajgiri.
